findings.location: approve-cost handler at epics.py:317-347; cost gate node manager.py:2036-2126; route manager.py:2532-2535
findings.finding: Epic cost approval is a deterministic dead-end loop (feature F-09 BROKEN). Clicking Approve cost sets epic.status='pending' and relaunches the SAME manager graph, whose _cost_estimate_node recomputes estimate_epic_cost(subtask_count=5, db=db) with unchanged inputs and, when estimate.requires_approval, sets the epic BACK to 'pending_cost_approval' with the same halt_reason and routes to END. No cost-approved signal is persisted or consumed anywhere ('cost_approved' = 0 grep hits in backend/). The user's approval click re-launches the manager and the epic reliably re-halts.
findings.evidence: FE button: apps/web/app/epics/[id]/page.tsx:151-154 -> lib/api.ts:376 approveCost -> POST /api/epics/{id}/approve-cost (epics.py:317). Handler: epics.py:329 status check, :338 epic.status='pending', :339 relaunch. Cost gate: manager.py:2036-2126; requires_approval branch :2062-2126; route _route_after_cost_estimate :2532-2535 ('pending_cost_approval' -> END). estimate_epic_cost is deterministic for fixed inputs (pipeline/cost_controller.py:139-198: historical averages or config coefficients, subtask_count=5 fixed at the call site). grep -rn 'cost_approved' backend/ -> 0 hits.
findings.production_impact: Any epic whose estimate exceeds settings.cost_approval_threshold can never proceed via the approval button; the only workaround is scope reduction below threshold or manual DB intervention. High-severity usability/flow defect, no data loss, no security impact.
findings.confidence: High (source-level deterministic trace; runtime UNVERIFIED in read-only mode)
findings.recommendation: Persist the approval (e.g., epic.cost_approved_by/at) and have _cost_estimate_node honor it (skip halt when an approval newer than the estimate exists), or remove the re-estimate on relaunch by passing a pre-approved flag through run_epic_manager.

findings.finding: On generic manager-pipeline exception the handler marks pipeline state 'blocked', appends a log and sends an alert but NEVER calls transition_task — unlike the success/blocked path above it and the launch_coder pattern (:1043-1048). The task is abandoned mid-state, breaking Journey E's terminal-state guarantee. This is merged finding H-1 (ARCH-01-001 = ORCH-04-101), re-verified OPEN at 90dac23b.
findings.evidence: agents.py:613-620 (except Exception -> update_pipeline_state(db2, task_id, 'blocked') + append_log + send_task_alert; no transition_task); contrast agents.py:1043-1048 and :257-277.
findings.production_impact: Tasks whose manager run crashes never reach a terminal task state; downstream lists/metrics/exports show them as live forever until manually reconciled.
findings.recommendation: Add the same terminal transition_task call used by the success path (accepted as known limitation in Audit 10; flagged here as the highest-priority one-liner).

findings.finding: The bhaskar agent is registered (AGENT_CONTRACT / discovery) but its role prompt file does not exist, so any routing to it resolves to an agent that cannot run — feature F-34 BROKEN. Cross-ref AGENT-02-001 (Audit 02); re-verified ABSENT at 90dac23b.
findings.evidence: ls backend/roles/ | grep -i bhaskar -> no match; 86 role files; AGENT-02-001 in json/AUDIT_02_AGENTS.json.
findings.production_impact: Specialized routing that selects bhaskar fails at run time (no role instructions); bounded to that agent's paths.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing role file or remove the agent from the registry/dispatch map.
